NDT training in Boston: how it works for Boston employers and technicians

Short answer: NDT training for Boston-area technicians is ASNT SNT-TC-1A based. Your employer's written practice sets the rules; you complete formal classroom training for the method and level, log supervised on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered under a Level III, and pass an annual vision test. Atlantis NDT delivers Level I, II and III training live online or onsite at your Boston-area facility, with no travel to a training centre.

Greater Boston is not a refinery town, and that shapes what NDT training here has to look like. The inspection work in eastern Massachusetts is spread across jet-engine manufacturing on the North Shore, submarine and naval work at the shipyards that ring New England, fuel and LNG terminals along the Mystic River and Chelsea Creek, bioprocess and pharmaceutical piping in Cambridge and along Route 128, bridges and transit structures owned by MassDOT and the MBTA, and a growing offshore-wind supply chain on the South Coast. Each of those sectors writes different acceptance criteria into its contracts, so a Boston technician who only knows one code tends to hit a ceiling quickly.

This section explains the training and certification path in practical terms: which methods Boston employers actually ask for, how the SNT-TC-1A steps fit together, how online and onsite delivery work around New England schedules, what radiography crews need from the Massachusetts Radiation Control Program, and what an employer needs in place before a single technician can be certified. For the wider programme overview see our NDT training programmes.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Boston

Every course below is built on the ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice and on the body of knowledge used by Level III examiners. Courses can be run as individual enrolments on live online cohorts, or as a closed group for a single Boston employer, delivered at the employer's shop, plant or yard. Level III candidates can add ASNT Level III exam preparation for the Basic and method examinations.

MethodLevelsWhat Boston employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, IIIThickness surveys on terminal tanks and piping, weld examination on structural steel and bridge members, forging and bar-stock inspection for aerospace suppliersLevel I: none beyond employer requirements. Level II: Level I training and experience per the written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, IIIWeld examination on fabricated structures, offshore-wind secondary steel, and complex aerospace geometries where encoded data is requiredConventional UT background is normally required by the written practice
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, IIICrack sizing and weld volumetric examination on thick-section vessels and heavy fabrications as an RT alternativeConventional UT background
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, IIIPipe and vessel welds at fuel terminals and power plants, castings, and film or digital interpretation for fabrication shopsRadiation safety training and state requirements apply in addition to SNT-TC-1A training
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, IIISurface crack detection on welds, lifting gear, crane components and ferrous castings in shipyard and structural workNone beyond employer requirements for Level I
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, IIINon-ferrous and stainless components, including aerospace parts and stainless process piping in pharmaceutical facilitiesNone beyond employer requirements for Level I

Two notes that matter in the Boston market. First, aerospace suppliers that feed engine and airframe primes usually work to an aerospace qualification standard such as NAS 410 on top of, or instead of, SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis training is SNT-TC-1A based; it gives you the method knowledge and hands-on skill, but the aerospace employer's own qualification scheme decides how that training is credited. Second, pharmaceutical and biotech owners in Cambridge and along Route 128 specify ASME BPE for hygienic piping, where visual and borescope examination of orbital welds is central. A strong VT Level II course, with borescope practice, maps directly to that work.

If you are not sure which method to start with, request a Boston training quote and tell us which industry you work in; we will suggest a sequence that matches what local employers hire for.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Boston, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is a recommended practice, not a licence. Certification is issued by your employer, and the employer's written practice is the controlling document. That is why two Boston companies can certify technicians in slightly different ways and both be compliant. The sequence below is the one almost every written practice follows.

  1. Employer written practice. Your employer adopts a written practice that defines levels, training hours, experience, examinations, vision requirements and recertification for each method. If you are an independent technician, the company you work for at the time of certification is the certifying employer.
  2. Formal classroom training. You complete documented training for the method and level. Minimum hours are set in the written practice, usually based on the SNT-TC-1A tables; see our training requirements matrix for the reference figures by method and level rather than relying on hearsay.
  3. On-the-job experience. You log supervised experience in the method. Experience must be documented, and the written practice defines how it is counted when a technician works in more than one method.
  4. General examination. A written test on the principles and theory of the method.
  5. Specific examination. A written test on the equipment, procedures, codes and acceptance criteria the employer actually uses, for example the ASME Section V techniques and the Section VIII or B31.3 acceptance criteria your Boston clients specify.
  6. Practical examination. A hands-on test on real specimens with known discontinuities, administered and graded under a Level III.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast checks, repeated annually.
  8. Certification. The employer's Level III (or the employer, on the Level III's recommendation) issues the certification and keeps the records.
  9. Recertification. Certification lapses on the interval set by the written practice, and also when a technician changes employer. Recertification is by examination or by documented continuing performance, depending on the written practice.

The employer-based model has a practical consequence for Boston technicians who move between contractors: your training certificates and experience logs travel with you, but your certification does not. Keep copies of everything. A new employer's Level III can recognise your previous training and experience and re-examine you under their written practice. For a fuller explanation read our SNT-TC-1A certification guide.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Boston crews

Atlantis NDT does not operate a physical training centre in Boston or anywhere else in Massachusetts. Instead, training is delivered in two ways that suit how New England companies work.

Live online. Theory for every method and level runs as live, instructor-led sessions that technicians join from home or the office. This covers the general and much of the specific body of knowledge, including code interpretation. It is the practical option for individual technicians and for small shops that cannot release a whole crew at once. See online NDT training for how sessions and assessments are structured.

Onsite at your facility. For a Boston-area employer with several technicians, the most efficient format is usually onsite training at your own shop, plant or yard, under ASNT Level III oversight. Trainees practise on your equipment, your procedures and, where possible, your own specimens, which makes the specific and practical examinations far more relevant. This is how most corporate programmes run; see corporate NDT training.

Scheduling around New England work patterns. Several Boston-area sectors have predictable peaks. Outdoor bridge and structural work concentrates in the warmer months and slows sharply in winter, which makes January to March a natural training window for field crews. Power plants in the region schedule refuelling or maintenance outages that pull inspectors off training. Shipyard and naval work follows availability schedules set by the customer. Tell us your blackout dates and we will build the cohort around them. Cohort and onsite quotes are returned within one business day; ask about onsite training for your Boston crew.

Where NDT technicians work in Boston

The eastern Massachusetts inspection market is broad rather than dominated by one industry. These are the main employer sectors and what they tend to ask for.

  • Aerospace and jet engines. GE Aerospace's Lynn plant on the North Shore builds military and helicopter engines, and a network of machine shops, forging and coating suppliers across Massachusetts and southern New Hampshire serves engine and airframe primes. These employers rely heavily on PT, MT, ET and UT, and usually qualify personnel under an aerospace standard such as NAS 410 alongside supplier requirements. Nadcap accreditation is common among the suppliers.
  • Naval shipbuilding and repair. Portsmouth Naval Shipyard in Kittery, Maine, and General Dynamics Electric Boat's yards at Groton, Connecticut and Quonset Point, Rhode Island, sit within commuting or weekly-travel range of Boston. Naval work is done to NAVSEA technical publications for NDT and welding, which impose their own qualification requirements; SNT-TC-1A training is a common foundation but technicians should expect additional naval-specific qualification from the yard or prime.
  • Fuel and LNG terminals. The Everett LNG import terminal on the Mystic River and the petroleum tank farms along Chelsea Creek and the Mystic supply heating oil, jet fuel for Logan Airport and road fuels to much of New England. Tank floor, shell and nozzle inspection, piping thickness surveys and weld RT are routine, typically to API standards for tanks and piping.
  • Power generation. Seabrook Station in New Hampshire and Millstone in Connecticut are the operating nuclear plants in the region, and there are gas-fired combined-cycle plants throughout Massachusetts. Pilgrim, in Plymouth, is being decommissioned. Nuclear work follows ASME Section XI and the plant's own qualification programmes; conventional plants use ASME Section I, V and B31.1.
  • Biotech and pharmaceutical process piping. Cambridge, Boston's Seaport and the Route 128 and I-495 corridors host dense clusters of biomanufacturing plants. Hygienic stainless piping built to ASME BPE depends on orbital welding with visual and borescope examination, plus PT and RT where specified.
  • Bridges, transit and structures. MassDOT, the MBTA and municipal owners maintain a large stock of steel bridges, many of them old enough to need fatigue-crack inspection. Structural steel fabrication follows AWS D1.1, and bridge fabrication follows AWS D1.5, with UT, MT and VT as the working methods.
  • Offshore wind. New Bedford's Marine Commerce Terminal and Salem have been used as staging and marshalling ports for projects off the Massachusetts coast, bringing demand for weld and coating inspection on secondary steel and port infrastructure.

Radiography licensing in Massachusetts. Massachusetts is an NRC Agreement State, so industrial radiography using radioactive sources is licensed and inspected by the Radiation Control Program in the Massachusetts Department of Public Health rather than directly by the NRC. Radiographers working with sources must meet the state's industrial radiography requirements, which parallel the federal 10 CFR Part 34 model: radiation safety training, a recognised radiographer certification, and supervised work under the licensee's radiation safety programme. Crews that also work in New Hampshire, Rhode Island or Maine should check each state programme's requirements, as all four are Agreement States with their own rules. SNT-TC-1A RT training covers image quality, technique and interpretation; it does not replace the state radiation safety requirements.

Boilers and pressure vessels. Massachusetts has its own boiler and pressure vessel regulations and inspection regime, and owners typically require ASME Code work to be examined by certified personnel under a documented written practice. What local employers most often ask for, in our experience of reviewing job requirements, is a current SNT-TC-1A Level II in at least two methods, clear documentation of training hours and experience, and familiarity with the codes their clients name in contracts. For earnings context, see our NDT salary guide.

Level III services and written practices for Boston NDT companies

Many Boston-area NDT users are small: a fabrication shop in Worcester County, an aerospace machine shop on the North Shore, a specialist bridge inspection firm, or a biotech contractor that suddenly needs certified VT inspectors. These companies often have capable technicians but no written practice, no Level III, and no clean audit trail. That gap usually surfaces during a customer audit or a code inspector's visit.

Atlantis NDT supports employers in three ways:

  • Written practice development. We draft a written practice tailored to your methods, levels and client codes, covering training, experience, examinations, vision testing, records and recertification. See written practice development.
  • Outside Level III services. An ASNT Level III can prepare and grade examinations, review procedures and techniques, and sign certifications on your behalf under your written practice, which is how many small Boston employers stay compliant without hiring a full-time Level III.
  • Procedure and technique review. Method procedures aligned to ASME Section V, AWS D1.1 and D1.5, and your clients' specifications, so technicians are examined on what they actually do.

If an audit is coming, book a Level III consultation and we will review your current documentation first. More background is in our SNT-TC-1A guidance.

Practise before the practical exam

The practical examination is where many candidates struggle, especially technicians who learned the theory online and have had limited time on real equipment. Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. Boston trainees heading into aerospace or terminal work can rehearse set-up, scanning discipline and indication recognition in settings that resemble their future jobs.

The simulator is a practice tool only. It does not replace the practical examination, which must be performed on real specimens with real equipment and graded under a Level III, and it does not count toward documented on-the-job experience unless your employer's written practice says otherwise. Use it to arrive at the practical exam more confident, not to skip it.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He oversees course content, examinations and onsite programmes, and works directly with employers on written practices and Level III services.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Boston

How do I get NDT certified in Boston?

Under SNT-TC-1A you are certified by your employer. You complete formal training for the method and level, log supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations under a Level III, and pass a vision test. If you are not yet employed in NDT, start with Level I training in a high-demand method such as UT, MT or PT, then apply to Boston-area inspection companies, fabricators or aerospace suppliers who will certify you under their written practice.

Can I take NDT training online in Massachusetts?

Yes. Theory for all methods and levels is available as live online instruction, which suits technicians anywhere in Massachusetts or neighbouring New England states. Practical skills and the practical examination still require hands-on work with real equipment and specimens, which is arranged onsite with your employer or as part of an employer programme. See online NDT training.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the written practice your employer follows and on whether you already hold UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom hours and experience for each level, and most employers adopt those figures. Check the training requirements matrix for the reference numbers, and remember that the experience requirement usually takes longer to satisfy than the classroom portion.

Do I need a license for radiography in Massachusetts?

The company needs a radioactive materials licence from the Massachusetts Radiation Control Program to perform source-based radiography, and individual radiographers must meet the state's training and certification requirements for industrial radiography. X-ray equipment is registered separately. SNT-TC-1A RT certification covers technique and interpretation, not radiation safety compliance, so you need both. Always confirm current requirements with the state programme.

What does NDT training cost in Boston?

We do not publish prices. The quote depends on method, level, group size, and whether training is online or onsite at your Boston-area facility. Individual and cohort quotes are returned within one business day; request your Boston NDT training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Boston employers?

SNT-TC-1A is the most widely used personnel qualification basis for US industrial NDT, and Boston-area fabricators, terminals, inspection contractors and many power and structural owners work to it. Aerospace suppliers commonly qualify personnel under NAS 410 and naval work follows NAVSEA requirements; in those sectors SNT-TC-1A training is a strong foundation but the employer applies its own scheme on top.

Which NDT method should I learn first for Boston jobs?

For structural, bridge and fabrication work, UT and MT with VT are the core. For aerospace suppliers, PT, MT and ET are the most common entry methods. For terminals and power plants, UT thickness and weld inspection plus RT. Many technicians start with PT and MT, which are shorter and open doors quickly, then add UT.

Do Boston biotech and pharma plants hire NDT technicians?

They hire inspection personnel, often through contractors, for hygienic piping built to ASME BPE. Visual and borescope examination of orbital welds is the main requirement, with PT and RT where the specification calls for them. A VT Level II with strong borescope skills is directly relevant.

Can you train our whole crew onsite in Massachusetts?

Yes. Onsite programmes run at the employer's facility under ASNT Level III oversight, using your equipment and procedures. They can be scheduled around outages, winter shutdowns or project peaks. See corporate NDT training.

Does Atlantis offer API 653, CWI or NAS 410 courses in Boston?

No. Atlantis training is ASNT SNT-TC-1A based only. Some Boston employers also ask for API inspector certificates, AWS CWI or NAS 410 qualification; those are separate schemes administered by other bodies and employers.

I am a Level II. How do I become a Level III in Boston?

Level III requires significant experience plus passing the ASNT Level III Basic and method examinations, or an equivalent employer examination under the written practice. Our ASNT Level III exam preparation covers the Basic and method content, and practice questions such as our UT Level 2 practice questions help candidates at every level.

Does my certification transfer if I change employers in Boston?

Not automatically. SNT-TC-1A certification belongs to the employer. Your training records and experience logs are yours, and your new employer's Level III can credit them and re-examine you under the new written practice.
